en: Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī said this to the Blessed One: "If, Venerable Sir, there is the possibility for women to attain the fourth fruit of asceticism, may women receive the going-forth and full ordination into the state of a bhikṣuṇī within the well-expounded Dharma and Vinaya; may women practice [the religious life]."
When it was said, "The holy life in the presence of the Blessed One," the Blessed One said this to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī:

"In this very way, Gautamī, being shaven-headed and clad in the saṃghāṭī robe, lead the holy life—exclusive, complete, pure, and stainless—for as long as life lasts; that will be for your benefit for a long time."
"For the sake of, for the benefit of, and for the happiness of [the community]," Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī said this to the Blessed One a second and even a third time:
"Venerable Sir, if there is the possibility for women to attain the fourth fruit of asceticism, may they receive it."

"Let women practice the holy life in the presence of the Blessed One under the well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya, undertaking the going-forth, the full ordination, and the state of a bhikṣuṇī"— thus the Blessed One spoke this to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī a second and even a third time.

"In this very way, Gautamī, you—shaven-headed and clad in the *saṃghāṭī* robe—should practice for as long as life lasts the celibate life (*brahmacarya*) that is exclusively, perfectly fulfilled, pure, and cleansed; that will be for your benefit, welfare, and happiness for a long time.
Then Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī, having been refused by the Blessed One even up to three times, bowed her head at the feet of the Blessed One and departed from his presence.
Then Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī, standing at the edge outside the gateway chamber, wept, shedding tears.
The Venerable Ānanda saw Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī standing at the edge outside the gateway chamber, weeping and shedding tears; having seen her, he then said this to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī:
"Why, Gautamī, do you stand alone at the edge of the outer gate-chamber, weeping and shedding tears?
She replied: "Venerable Ānanda, it is because women do not obtain the going-forth, the full ordination, or the status of a bhikṣuṇī within this well-expounded Dharma and Vinaya.
"In that case, Gautamī, wait here while I go to see the Blessed One."
Then the venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, he stood to one side.
Standing to one side, the venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
"If, Venerable Sir, there is the possibility for a woman to attain the fourth fruit of asceticism, may she receive it."

“If women were to go forth in this well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya, to receive full ordination, and to attain the status of a bhikṣuṇī, they would lead the holy life in the presence of the Blessed One.
Therefore, Ānanda, let it not please you that women go forth in this well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya; let them not receive full ordination, nor attain the status of a bhikṣuṇī.”

For what reason? Because, Ānanda, in whatever Dharma and Vinaya women go forth, that Dharma and Vinaya does not endure for long. Just as, Ānanda, a family with many women and few men becomes easily assailable and very vulnerable to robbers and thieves, even so, Ānanda, in whatever Dharma and Vinaya women go forth, that Dharma and Vinaya does not endure for long.
It is just as if, Ānanda, lightning were to strike a householder farmer’s abundant field of rice, turning it double-curved [and causing] the destruction, ruin, and calamity of that very rice.
In the same way, Ānanda, in whatever Dharma and Vinaya women go forth, that Dharma and Vinaya does not endure for long.
It is just as if, Ānanda, a disease called *mañjiṣṭhikā* were to afflict a householder farmer’s abundant field of sugarcane.

It would fall [to ruin], even for the uprooting, destruction, and calamity of this very sugarcane field; in exactly the same way, Ānanda, in whatever Dharma and Vinaya women go forth, that Dharma and Vinaya does not endure for long.
However, Ānanda, I prescribe eight weighty rules (gurudharma) for women as a restriction and so they may not transgress them, in which the women must train for as long as life lasts.

It is just as if, Ānanda, a householder farmer at the end of the rainy season, in the time of autumn, were to build a dam at the mouth of a river or at the mouth of a canal, solely for the purpose of obstructing the water and preventing its overflow. In the same way, Ānanda, I prescribe eight weighty rules (gurudharma) for women, for the purpose of obstruction and non-transgression, in which the womenfolk must train their lives long.
Which eight?
Ānanda, from the presence of the monks, the going forth, the full ordination, and the status of a bhikṣuṇī are to be sought by women.
Ānanda, I prescribe this first heavy rule for women as an obstacle so that it may not be transgressed.
In this regard, Ānanda, the female community must observe the training for as long as life lasts.
A bhikṣuṇī, Ānanda, must seek instruction and admonition from a bhikṣu every half-month.
This, Ānanda, I prescribe as the second heavy rule (gurudharma) for the female community, as an obstacle to prevent transgression.
In this regard, Ānanda, a woman must observe the training for as long as she lives.
A nun, Ānanda, must not enter the rains retreat in a residence where there is no monk.
This, Ānanda, I prescribe as the third heavy rule for women, as an obstacle and for the sake of non-transgression, wherein a woman must observe the training for as long as she lives.
Ānanda, a bhikṣuṇī who has completed her year of residence must invite the dual saṃgha by means of three grounds: what has been seen, what has been heard, or what is suspected.
Ānanda, I hereby prescribe this as the fourth heavy rule for women, as an obstacle and for the sake of non-transgression.
In this regard, the training must be observed by a woman for as long as she lives.
Ānanda, a nun must not reproach or remind a monk of a failure in morality, a failure in view, a failure in conduct, or a failure in livelihood. Ānanda, it is forbidden for a nun to reproach a monk.

To cause him to remember, by means of a failure in morality, a failure in view, a failure in conduct, or a failure in livelihood, one may accuse and remind a monk or a nun who is unobstructed [by the obstacles]. Ānanda, this I proclaim as the fifth *gurudharma* for women, as an obstruction so that they do not overstep it.
In this regard, the female community must observe the training rules for as long as life lasts.
Ānanda, a nun must not revile, provoke to anger, or abuse a monk.
Ānanda, it is forbidden for a bhikṣuṇī to revile, provoke to anger, or abuse a bhikṣu. Ānanda,
I hereby prescribe this sixth *gurudharma* for women as a restriction that must not be transgressed, in which women must practice the training for as long as they live.
"Ānanda, the nun Ānandā, having been taught the weighty dharmas, must undergo the *mānāpya* penance before both Saṅghas every half-month.
Ānanda, I hereby prescribe this as the seventh weighty dharma for women, as an obstruction and for the purpose of non-transgression, in which the women must train for as long as they live."

Ānanda, a nun who has been ordained for a hundred years must perform the acts of salutation, prostration, rising to greet, joining the palms, and respectful homage toward a monk ordained on that very same day.
Ānanda, I hereby prescribe this eighth *gurudharma* for women, as an obstacle and to prevent transgression, in which women must train their lives long.

“Ānanda, if Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī shall live having undertaken these eight weighty rules (gurudharma), that itself will be her going forth, that itself her full ordination, and that itself her state as a bhikṣuṇī.

Then the Venerable Ānanda, having rejoiced and delighted in the words spoken by the Blessed One, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and departed from the presence of the Blessed One. Thereupon, the Venerable Ānanda approached where Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī was.
Having approached Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī, he said this to her:
"Gautamī, the female sex has obtained the going-forth, the full ordination, and the status of a bhikṣuṇī within the well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya.
However, Gautamī, eight rules of respect have been prescribed for the female sex by the Blessed One."
"Regarding that which constitutes an obstruction and from which there is no transgression, wherein a woman must practice the training for as long as life lasts—we shall teach it;
you will understand.
"Speak, Venerable Ānanda, I shall listen."
The Blessed One said this to Gautamī: "Ānanda, from among the monks, the female community should expect ordination, full admission, and the status of a bhikṣuṇī.
This, Gautamī, is the first heavy rule (gurudharma) prescribed by the Blessed One for the female community.
"For the sake of restraint and for not transgressing, this training must be observed by a woman for as long as she lives.

The Blessed One said thus to Gautamī: 'Ānanda, a nun must seek instruction and admonition from the monks every half-month. This, Gautamī, is the second *gurudharma* for women established by the Blessed One."
It has been prescribed as an obstruction that cannot be transgressed, wherein a woman must observe the training for as long as life lasts.
Thus spoke the Blessed One to Gautamī.
"Ānanda, a nun must not enter the rains retreat in a residence where there is no monk; this, Gautamī, is the third *gurudharma* prescribed by the Blessed One for women,
as an obstruction and an unsurpassable rule which must be observed by women for as long as they live."
The Blessed One said this to Gautamī: "Ānanda, a bhikṣuṇī who has completed the rains retreat must perform the invitation ceremony (pravāraṇā) before both saṃghas on three grounds:

what is seen, what is heard, and what is suspected. Gautamī, this is the fourth heavy rule (gurudharma) prescribed by the Blessed One for women, as an obstacle and for non-transgression, which must be observed by women for as long as they live."
This training is to be observed.
The Blessed One said this, O Gautamī: "Ānanda, a nun must not reprove or remind a monk of a failure in morality, a failure in view, a failure in conduct, or a failure in livelihood."
"Ānanda, a bhikṣuṇī is restricted from accusing or reminding a bhikṣu regarding failure in morality, failure in view, failure in conduct, or failure in livelihood;

whereas a bhikṣu is not restricted from accusing or reminding a bhikṣuṇī regarding failure in morality, failure in view, failure in conduct, or failure in livelihood. Gautamī, this is the fifth weighty rule for women laid down by the Blessed One."
This has been prescribed as a restraint and an unsurpassable rule, wherein a woman must practice the training for as long as life lasts.
The Blessed One said this to Gautamī:
"Ānanda, a nun must not revile a monk, nor incite him to anger, nor abuse him."
"Ānanda, a bhikṣuṇī is forbidden from reviling, inciting anger in, or censuring a bhikṣu.
Thus, Gautamī, this sixth *gurudharma* has been prescribed by the Blessed One for women;
it is an obstruction and an unsurpassable rule which must be observed by women for as long as they live."
The Blessed One said this to Gautamī:
"Ānanda, a bhikṣuṇī who has committed an offense against a heavy rule (gurudharma) must undergo the *mānāpya* penance before both Saṃghas every half-month.
Gautamī, this is the seventh heavy rule prescribed by the Blessed One for women, as an obstacle and so that they may not transgress."
In this regard, Gautamī, the Blessed One has said:

"Ānanda, even a bhikṣuṇī who has been ordained for a hundred years must perform the acts of salutation, prostration, rising to greet, joining of palms, and respectful homage toward a bhikṣu ordained on that very same day. This, Gautamī, is [the rule]."

[The admission into the order, the full ordination, and the status of a bhikṣuṇī] for the five hundred Śākyāyanīs headed by Gautamī occurred through their acceptance of the eight *gurudharma*s; for other women, it occurs according to the gradual sequence.

When any woman approaches any bhikṣuṇī, she should be questioned by her regarding the obstructing factors; having been questioned, she should be made to take them up, and once they have taken them up, the three goings for refuge and the five precepts of a laywoman (upāsikā) should be given to her.
What are the goings for refuge? They are: the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha.
What are the five precepts?

They are: abstaining from taking life, abstaining from taking what is not given, abstaining from sexual misconduct, abstaining from false speech, and abstaining from fermented and distilled liquors and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence.
Furthermore, the precepts for going for refuge should be conferred in this manner.

Having first performed the three circumambulations, having caused her to pay homage to the Teacher, and having caused her to join her palms in *añjali*, one should cause her to pay homage and join her palms in *añjali* before giving her the precepts for going for refuge. Then she herself should speak as follows: "Pay heed, Noble Lady; I, [name], from this day forward for as long as life lasts..."
I go for refuge to the Buddha, the Blessed One, the foremost of bipeds;
I go for refuge to the Dharma, the foremost of those free from passion;
I go for refuge to the Saṅgha, the foremost of assemblies.
In this manner, a second and a third time, the five precepts (*śikṣāpada*) should then be conferred:
"Pay attention, Noble Lady (*āryikā*): just as the Noble Ones, the Arhats, for as long as life lasts, having abandoned the taking of life, [abstain] from the taking of life..."
Having desisted from [taking life], I, so-and-so, from this day forward for as long as life lasts, having abandoned the taking of life,
abstain from the taking of life; by this first limb, I train after the training of those noble Arhats, I conform to it, and I imitate it.
Furthermore, just as those noble Arhats, for as long as life lasts, having abandoned taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech,

and the occasion of negligence consisting of fermented and distilled liquors and intoxicants, have abstained from the occasion of negligence consisting of fermented and distilled liquors and intoxicants— even so I, [name], from this day forward for as long as life lasts, shall abandon taking what is not given and sexual misconduct...

"Having abandoned false speech and the occasion for negligence consisting of fermented and distilled liquors and intoxicants, I abstain from the occasion for negligence consisting of fermented and distilled liquors and intoxicants.
By this fifth limb, I train after the training of those noble Arhats, I conform to it, and I imitate it. May the noble ladies accept me as a female lay follower (*upāsikā*).
Thus it should be said.
Thus a second time and a third time.
A nun who has gone for the three refuges and maintains the five precepts should say, "It is appropriate.
She should reply, "Very well."
Thereafter, a nun who shall announce [the matter] in the midst of the Saṃgha must be requested.
Once she has been requested, that nun must be questioned by her [who made the request]:
"Have you been asked about these obstructive factors?"
If she announces [the matter] without having asked [permission], she incurs an offense of transgression (*sātisāra*).

Then, when the community of nuns (*bhikṣuṇī-saṃgha*) has sat down and assembled, she—whether by counting in order or being one seeking ordination—should perform the proper salutation (*sāmīcī*) at the end of the seniority row; having made her sit in the squatting posture (*utkuṭuka*) with palms joined (*añjali*) raised, she should be placed facing the assembly.
This should be announced:
"May the noble Saṃgha of nuns listen!
This woman named so-and-so, a householder clad in white garments with her hair not yet shorn, who seeks the going-forth under the one named so-and-so, desires [ordination]."
"In this well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya, let this woman named so-and-so, having shaved off her hair and donned saffron robes,
go forth from the home to the homeless life with perfect faith under the preceptor-nun named so-and-so; let her go forth."
It must be stated by all [the nuns]: "If she is pure, let her go forth.
If they say this, it is well; if they do not say this, they become guilty of an offense.
Thereafter, the preceptor-nun (upādhyāyikā) is to be requested; she is to be requested again in this manner:

Having performed the proper salutation, sitting before her in the squatting posture and joining the palms in reverence, she should speak as follows: "Pay attention, Preceptor; I, [name], request the Preceptor to be my Upādhyāyikā. May the Preceptor be my Upādhyāyikā;
through the Preceptor as Upādhyāyikā, I shall go forth."
Thus a second time, and likewise a third time.
Then the preceptor-ni should request a nun who removes hair to remove [the candidate's] hair.
While she is removing the hair, she must ask: "Sister, shall the hair be removed?
If she says, "Let it be removed," then it should be removed.
If she says, "No," he should say, "In that case, go.
Monks, I shall prescribe the rules of proper conduct for a nun who shaves the hair. A nun who shaves the hair should, if it is the cold season, bathe her with warm water;
if it is the hot season, she should bathe her with cold water.

If a nun who is having her hair shaved does not undertake and abide by the rules of customary conduct as they have been prescribed, she commits an offense. After the limbs have been shaved for a short while, the preceptor-nun herself must then give the saffron robes;
she, in turn, must receive them while prostrating at [the preceptor's] feet.

The lower garment should be put on. While putting it on, one should examine the private parts to ensure that she is not without private parts, nor possessing both sets of private parts, nor having deformed private parts.
They strip them naked and examine them, causing them shame.
The Blessed One said:
"One must not examine them by stripping them naked."
Furthermore, while she is being clothed, it must be examined without her being aware of it.

Thus, if she is found to be pure, then, having given her the saffron-colored robes, the preceptoress (upādhyāyikā) should grant her the going forth (pravrajyā), preceded by the taking of the three refuges.
Having prostrated at her feet and joined her palms in reverence, she should say:
"Pay heed, Preceptor; I, [name], from this day forward for as long as life lasts, go for refuge to the Buddha, the Blessed One, the foremost of two-legged beings;
I go for refuge to the Dharma, the best of those free from passion."

I go for refuge to the Saṅgha, the most excellent of assemblies. I follow in the renunciation of that Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Lion of the Śākyas, the Sovereign King of the Śākyas, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha;
I renounce the marks of a householder.
I take up the marks of the going-forth;
having taken them up, I shall abide in them.
For the sake of the goal, I mention my name: [Name], with [Name] as my preceptor.
Thus a second time, and likewise a third time.
Then the preceptor-nun must be requested by her [the candidate]; she who shall grant the novice nun the training rules must be asked as follows:
"You have been asked about the obstructing factors.
If she bestows [the ordination] without having asked, she incurs an offense of transgression.
She who has been requested must cause her to perform a prostration to the Teacher and then...

...thereupon the robes must be formally determined (*adhiṣṭhātavya*). Pay attention, Preceptor (*upādhyāyikā*): I, named so-and-so, determine this robe as an outer cloak (*saṃghāṭī*); it is a robe that has been finished, is permissible, and is fit for use.
Thus a second time and a third time.
In this manner, the upper robe, the inner robe, the small bag, and the side-covering cloth are to be formally authorized.
Then, the alms bowl is to be presented to the community of nuns with these words:
"Pay attention, Venerable Lady! This is the bowl of the Venerable [Name]; let it not be deficient, nor excessive, nor too pale."
And all the bhikṣuṇīs should say, "It is beautiful; it is a good bowl.
Then the bowl is to be consecrated: having placed the bowl in the left hand and covered it with the right hand, one should say:
"Pay attention, Preceptor! I, [name], consecrate this bowl—the vessel of the sages, the vessel for alms—as fit for food and as fit for use."
Thus a second time and a third time.

Thereafter, having moved away from the vicinity of the ascetics and toward the vicinity of the [lay] visitors, she should bow her body, join her palms in *añjali*, and be made to stand facing the assembly. Then, the officiating nun (*karmakārikā*) should speak as follows:
"Who has been requested to be the secret instructor for [the candidate] named so-and-so? She who has been requested should say, "I am [the nun] named so-and-so.
Then, the officiating nun should first encourage her.
"Are you able, [Name], to instruct [Name] in secret with [Name] as preceptor?
If she is able, she should say, "I am able.
Then the officiating nun should perform the formal motion (*jñapti*) regarding Muktikā.
May the community of noble nuns listen: this nun named So-and-so has been appointed as the private instructor for the nun named So-and-so by the preceptor named So-and-so.
This nun named So-and-so is capable of instructing the nun named So-and-so in private with the preceptor named So-and-so.
If it is the right time for the community of noble nuns and if it pleases them, may the community of noble nuns authorize the nun named So-and-so.
One should appoint a private instructor:
"This nun, so-and-so, shall be the private instructor who will instruct so-and-so in secret, with so-and-so as her preceptor. This is the formal motion (*jñapti*).
Then, the nun who instructs in secret, having gone aside to a private place, should have her sit down in front of her in the squatting posture and make her join her palms; she should then say:
"Listen, [Name], this is the time for truth, the time for what is real. Whatever I ask you, [you must answer]."
All of that must be spoken by you with confidence: what is factual as factual, and what is not factual as not factual, and what is to be confessed as such.
You are a woman; you have lived as a householder for twelve years, or you are a young girl who has reached twenty years of age; your five robes and bowl are complete.
They are complete.
"Are your mother and father living? Or does your husband live? Have you been authorized by your mother and father, or authorized by your husband? Are you a slave? She should reply, "No."
Let there be no taking by force; let there be no selling; let there be no acquisition.
She must not be one who is subject to verbal censure; she must not be a magical creation; she must not be a royal servant.
Do not be one who commits an offense against the king; do not be one who performs acts harmful to the king.
Have you not committed or caused to be committed any act harmful to the king?
Are you not fierce, nor stricken by grief, nor pregnant, nor lacking sexual characteristics, nor possessing both sets of sexual characteristics?

Let her not be one whose sexual organs are disfigured; let her not be one who constantly has a discharge of blood; let her not be one who lacks blood; let her not be one who possesses [only] the marks [of a woman].
Do not be one who corrupts monks;
do not be a matricide;
do not be a patricide.
May you not be one who causes the shedding of blood with a malicious mind toward a Tathāgata; may you not be a heretic, nor one who has entered the fold of heretics;
may you not be a thief.
Not one who has raised a banner; not one who lives in communion through theft;
not one who lives in a separate communion.
"Do not live with us! Have you not already gone forth [into homelessness]?
If she says, "I have gone forth," one should say, "Then go right away. If she says, "I have not gone forth," [one should say: "Do not live with us!"
It should be asked: "Have you now gone forth? Have you practiced the holy life correctly? [She replies: "I have.
"Have you requested from the community of nuns the training in the six rules and the six secondary rules for two years? [She replies: "I have."
"You have been requested; you have been trained for two years in the six rules and the six secondary rules. You have been trained in the training.
You must not give anything at all to anyone, whether little or much."
"What is your name? "I am named so-and-so. "What is the name of your preceptor?
"For the sake of formality, I mention her name: my preceptor is named so-and-so.
"Listen, [you] named so-and-so: indeed, such things as these occur for women."
Physical ailments of the body are as follows: leprosy, boils, ringworm, vitiligo, scabies, itch, itching, herpes, eczema, hiccups, vomiting,
hemorrhoids, fever, consumption, exhaustion, dizziness, and asthma.
Cough, consumption, epilepsy, jaundice, and anemia.
Elephantiasis, hemorrhagic fever, fistula-in-ano, and burning sensations in the limbs.
Burning pain in the sides,
piercing pain in the bones,
and the quotidian fever.
A fever that recurs every second day;
one that recurs every third day; one that recurs every fourth day.
[May there not be] fever arising from the combination of humors, nor continuous fever; may such bodily afflictions, or any others of this kind, not exist in your body.
If she is pure, the private instructor should say to her:
"Whatever you have been asked by me, that very thing must be spoken by you in the midst of the Saṃgha; stay, do not come unsummoned.
Then, while standing on the way, the private instructor should say:

"May the community of noble nuns listen: I have instructed the one named so-and-so regarding the secret obstructing factors. She declares herself to be pure with respect to those obstructing factors. Should she come? All the bhikṣuṇīs should say: "If she is pure, let her come."
If they say so, it is well; if they do not say so, they become guilty of an offense.
Then, having had her sit down in front of a nun acting as the ritual officiant (*karmakārikā*), she should request the formal restraint for the practice of celibacy (*brahmacaryopasthāna-saṃvara*).
May the noble community of nuns listen. I, [name], am seeking full ordination from the preceptor [name]. I, [name], [request it] from the noble community of nuns.
"I request the restraint of the preliminary stage of the holy life (*brahmacaryopasthānasaṃvṛti*).

For the sake of the purpose, I mention my name: may the community of noble nuns (*āryikāsaṃgha*) grant the restraint of the preliminary stage of the holy life to me, [named] so-and-so, by means of the preceptor-nun (*upādhyāyikā*) named so-and-so.
Out of compassion, may they do so out of compassion. Thus a second and a third time.

Then, having made a formal motion (*jñapti*) by a nun who performs the ritual act, the formal act (*karman*) should be performed as follows: "Listen, noble Saṃgha! This one named so-and-so is seeking full ordination from the preceptor named so-and-so. This one named so-and-so requests from the noble Saṃgha the formal authorization for the practice of celibacy (*brahmacaryopasthāna-saṃvṛti*), with the preceptor named so-and-so."

"If it seems timely to the noble community of nuns and if the noble community of nuns grants permission, may we ask her about the obstructing factors in the midst of the community"— this is the formal motion (*jñapti*).

Listen, [you] who are named so-and-so: this is your time for truth, this is your time for reality; whatever I ask you, all that must be spoken by you with confidence—truth as truth and what is not true as not true, and it must be confessed. You are a woman, a woman—as before, all this must be said.
"Are there no such bodily ailments or other [disorders] in your body? She should reply, "No.
Then the formal motion (*jñapti*) should be made:
"Listen, noble Saṃgha! This one named so-and-so is seeking full ordination from the preceptor named so-and-so."

A girl who has lived at home for twelve years, or one who is twenty years of age, whose five robes and bowl are complete, and who declares herself to be pure regarding the obstructing conditions— this woman, named so-and-so, requests from the community of noble nuns the formal authorization for the practice of the holy life (*brahmacaryopasthānasaṃvṛti*).

"O Noble Saṅgha, if it is the right time and the Noble Saṅgha permits, let the Noble Saṅgha grant the formal authorization for the practice of celibacy to [Name], with [Name] as her preceptor. This is the motion (*jñapti*). And the formal act (*karman*) should be performed in this manner."

May the community of noble nuns listen: this woman named so-and-so, who has lived at home for twelve years and is seeking full ordination under the preceptor named so-and-so—whether she is a maiden or one who has reached twenty years of age—is complete with the five robes and the alms bowl;
she declares herself pure regarding the obstructing conditions.
This venerable nun named so-and-so requests full ordination from the community of nuns with so-and-so as her preceptor. Therefore,

may the community of nuns grant the formal authorization for the practice of celibacy to this nun named so-and-so, with so-and-so as her preceptor, to whichever nuns it pleases to grant the formal authorization for the practice of celibacy to this nun named so-and-so, with so-and-so as her preceptor.
The preceptor should say: "Let those who do not approve of this remain silent; let those who do approve speak. This is the first formal proclamation (*karmavācanā*);
the second and third formal proclamations should be stated in the same manner."

The community of noble nuns has granted the formal authorization for the practice of celibacy to [Name] by means of [Name] as preceptor; this has been accepted and permitted by the community, since there is silence. Thus do I understand it to be.
Thereafter, when the entire community of monks has assembled and gathered, or when a group of ten monks has formed a circle, and the entire community of nuns has likewise assembled—(BhīKaVā 19a1)
When the final assembly of the twelve-member circle of bhikṣuṇīs has gathered,
she should sit on a small stool or a cushion before the officiating bhikṣu, join her palms in *añjali*, and request full ordination from both Saṅghas:
"May the venerable Saṅghas of both communities listen."

I, [name], for the sake of the purpose [of ordination], state my name; I, [name], am seeking full ordination from the preceptor [name]. Therefore, I, [name], request full ordination from both Sanghas.
May the venerable ones of both Sanghas grant me full ordination;
may the venerable ones of both Sanghas lift me up.
May the Venerable Saṅghas of both orders favor me;
may the Venerable Saṅghas of both orders have compassion for me.
Out of compassion, acting out of compassion;
thus a second and a third time.
Thereafter, the officiating monk shall perform the formal motion (*jñapti*):

"May the venerable members of both Saṅghas listen. This woman, named so-and-so, is seeking full ordination from the preceptor named so-and-so. This woman, named so-and-so, requests full ordination from both Saṅghas with the preceptor named so-and-so. If it is the pleasure of both Saṅghas..."
"The time has come; may both Saṅghas grant their permission that we may question her regarding the obstructing factors (antarāyika-dharma) in the midst of both Saṅghas. This is the motion (jñapti).
Listen, O [Name], this is the time for truth, the time for what is real:
whatever I ask you, [you must answer].

All of that must be spoken by you with confidence: what is true as true, and what is untrue as untrue, and it must be confessed: "I am a woman, a woman living at home for twelve years, or a maiden who has reached twenty years of age;
[I am] twenty years of age."
Your five robes and alms bowl are complete;
they are complete.
Your mother and father are living, or your master is living.
"Have you been permitted by your parents or your master?
"I have been permitted.
"Are you not a slave?"
For I am not one who takes by force,
nor one who sells,
nor one who speaks [falsely].
May she not be a courtesan; may she not be a royal servant;
may she not be one guilty of an offense against the king.

May you not have performed or caused to be performed any action detrimental to the king; may you not be fierce, nor stricken by grief, nor pregnant, nor lacking sexual organs, nor possessing both sets of organs, nor having disordered organs;
may you not be one whose blood flows constantly, nor one who has no blood at all.
May you not be a fortune-teller;
may you not be a corrupter of monks; may you not be a matricide.

Do not be a matricide; do not be a patricide; do not be one who, with a malicious mind, sheds the blood of a Tathāgata; do not be a heretic; do not be one who has entered into the life of a heretic; do not be a thief; do not be one who lives under a banner; do not be one who dwells in communion through theft; do not be one who dwells in a different communion.
"Are you not one who does not live in communion?
Have you previously gone forth? If she says, "I have gone forth," one should say, "In that case, go right away. If she says, "I have not gone forth," one should ask, "Have you now gone forth?
Have you practiced the holy life correctly?"
[Regarding] conduct:
Have you requested training in the six rules and the six secondary rules within the community of nuns for two years? [She replies: "I have."
You have been trained for two years in the six rules and the six secondary rules of training;

you have been trained. The formal authorization for the practice of celibacy has been granted to you by the community of nuns; the preliminary duties have been performed for you by the community of nuns; you have rendered service to the community of nuns.
The mind has been won over.
Are you completely pure or not?
You are completely pure.

"You must not give anything at all to anyone, whether little or much. What is your name? What is the name of your preceptor? "I am [name], and my preceptor is [name]. "I take your name for the sake of the matter; my preceptor is [name]. "Listen, [name]: indeed, such bodily afflictions as these occur in the bodies of women."
Namely: boils, leprosy, scabs, vitiligo, ringworm, itch, scratching, silver-colored spots, and eczema.
Hiccups, vomiting, and hemorrhoids.
Fever, high fever, and consumption.
Exhaustion, vertigo, coughing, dyspnea, wasting, and epilepsy.
Jaundice, anemia, and elephantiasis.
Hemorrhage,
fistula-in-ano,
burning sensation in the limbs, burning sensation in the sides, and piercing pain in the bones.
The quotidian, the tertian, the quartan, and the quaternian fevers.
"Is there a fever caused by the combination of all three humors (sānnipātika), or a continuous fever? Do such bodily ailments as these, or others, exist in your body?
Then she should speak according to the facts.
Then, after the monk acting as the proclaimer has made the formal motion (*jñapti*), the ritual act (*karman*) should be performed:

"May the venerable members of both Saṃghas listen! This woman named so-and-so, who is seeking full ordination from the preceptor named so-and-so, is a householder who has lived for twelve years, or she is a maiden who has reached twenty years of age; her five robes are complete."

The Saṅgha of bhikṣuṇīs has granted her the bowl; she has been trained for two years in the six rules and the six secondary rules. The Saṅgha of bhikṣuṇīs has granted her the formal authorization for the practice of the holy life according to the three rules. The Saṅgha of bhikṣuṇīs has performed for her the preliminary rites.
The mind of the community of nuns has been won over by this woman;

she declares herself to be pure regarding the obstructing factors. This woman, named so-and-so, requests full ordination from both communities with such-and-such a woman as her preceptor. If it is the right time for both communities and they should grant permission, [let it be done].
"May the dual Saṅgha ordain the one named so-and-so with the preceptor named so-and-so; this is the formal motion."
In this manner, the ritual action should be performed.

May the venerable members of both Saṃghas listen: this woman named so-and-so, who has lived at home for twelve years and seeks full ordination from the preceptor named so-and-so, is either a maiden of twelve years or one who has reached twenty years of age; her five robes and alms bowl are complete, and she has been granted [these] by the Bhikṣuṇī-saṃgha.

For two years she has trained in the training regarding the six rules and the six secondary rules; for two years she has been granted the training in the six rules and the six secondary rules by the community of nuns. By means of the three rules, the formal authorization for the practice of celibacy has been granted to her by the community of nuns. The preliminary duties have been performed by the community of nuns, and the mind of the community of nuns has been won over by her.

She declares herself to be pure regarding the obstructing factors. This woman, named so-and-so, requests full ordination from both Sanghas with such-and-such a name as preceptor. Therefore, let the Sangha of both communities grant full ordination to this woman, named so-and-so, with such-and-such a name as preceptor.
For those venerable ones who consent to granting full ordination to this woman, named so-and-so, with such-and-such a name as preceptor, [let them remain silent].

Those who do not approve [of this] should remain silent; those who do not approve should speak. This is the first formal proclamation (*karmavācanā*). In the same way, the second and third formal proclamations are to be recited.
"This woman, so-and-so, has been ordained by the dual Saṃgha through the preceptoress so-and-so. It is approved and permitted by the Saṃgha, since there is silence; thus do I hold it to be so.
Thereupon, the shadow must be measured.
The bhikṣuṇīs [should measure] with very long creepers.
They measured the shadow.
The Blessed One said:
"The shadow must not be measured by very long creepers."
They measured it with their feet.
The Blessed One said:
"It should not be measured with the feet."
Furthermore, it should be measured with a four-fingered wooden measure;
as many wooden measures as there are, so many men should be declared.
The communal agreement (sāmāyika) should be announced.
There are the winter, summer, rainy, late-rainy, and long-rainy periods. Among these,
the winter period consists of four months, the summer period consists of four months,
and the rainy period consists of one month.
The short rainy season lasts for one night and day;
the long rainy season lasts for three months minus one night.
The time must be announced.
The dawn at the beginning;
the dawn at midday;
the dawn at the end.
The sun has not yet risen;
the sun has risen; the sun has risen by one-eighth part.
When one quarter has risen,
it is midday;
when one quarter remains, it is the end of the day.
When one-eighth of the day remains;
when the sun has not yet set; when the sun has set.
"The stars have not yet risen," and so forth;
from that, three [cases arise]. (BhīKaVā 22b1)
The dependencies must be announced:

"Listen, O [Name], these three dependencies have been declared by that Blessed One—the one who knows, the one who sees, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One—for a bhikṣuṇī who has thus gone forth and received full ordination; relying upon which, for a bhikṣuṇī in the well-proclaimed [Dharma]..."
Going forth and receiving full ordination in the Dharma and Vinaya constitutes the state of a bhikṣuṇī.
What are the three?
Among robes, rag-robes are appropriate, easily obtained, and [easily maintained].
That depending upon which, for a bhikṣuṇī, there is going forth, full ordination, and the status of a bhikṣuṇī within this well-expounded Dharma and Vinaya:
"O [Name], are you able to subsist for as long as life lasts on robes made of discarded rags? "I am able."
An extra gain may be a cloth, or a garment, or a cloak, or fine silk, or linen, or silk, or *āmila*, or *somila*,
or *kṛmivarṇa*, or fine *kāśi* cloth, or fine *kṣaumaka* cloth, or fine *dukūlaka* cloth, or fine *koṭambaka* cloth;
or whatever other suitable robe (*cīvara*) might arise from the Saṅgha or from an individual.
In that regard, you must exercise moderation in accepting gifts.
Will you attain awakening in such a state?
"I shall attain it."

Listen, [Name], alms-food is the foremost of foods; it is permissible, easy to obtain, and by relying upon it, a nun attains the going-forth, the full ordination, and the status of a bhikṣuṇī within the well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya.
Are you able, [Name], to subsist on alms-food as your meal for as long as life lasts? I am able.
Excess acquisitions—

whether meals, refreshments, drinks of gruel, regular invitations, special invitations, those on the eighth day, those on the fourteenth day, or whatever other suitable food may arise from the Saṃgha.
Or, regarding the person from whom you receive it, you should exercise moderation even in that acceptance;
will you be able to fully comprehend such a situation?
"I shall fully comprehend it."
Listen, [you] named so-and-so: fermented urine is a suitable and easily obtainable medicine for medicinal purposes.

Relying upon this, do you, [you] named so-and-so, venture to undertake the going-forth, the full ordination, and the status of a bhikṣuṇī within the well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya? "I venture, [to maintain myself] throughout my life by means of fermented urine as medicine."
Excess acquisitions: ghee, oil, honey, molasses,
root medicine, stem medicine, leaf medicine, flower medicine, fruit medicine, [medicines] for a limited time, for a watch of the night, for seven days, and for life.

Furthermore, whatever other suitable medicine may arise from the Saṅgha or from an individual, you must exercise moderation in accepting it, thinking: "I shall surely avoid such a situation. Listen, [Name], these eight [cases] were taught by that Blessed One who knows and sees.

The Arhat, the Truly Self-Awakened One, has thus declared these *patanīya* (defeatable) dharmas for a nun who has gone forth and received full ordination; if a nun commits any one of these states, by that very commission she ceases to be a nun, ceases to be a *śramaṇī*, ceases to be a daughter of the Śākyas, and falls from the state of a nun— the state of being a *śramaṇa* is destroyed for her.
Her asceticism is destroyed, crushed, fallen, defeated, and beyond recovery—
just like a palm tree cut off at the crown;
it is incapable of becoming green again, and incapable of attaining growth, increase, or expansion.

In the same way, a bhikṣuṇī who commits any one of these eight offenses becomes, by that very commission, no longer a bhikṣuṇī, no longer a śramaṇī, no longer a daughter of the Śākyas; she falls from the state of a bhikṣuṇī. Her status as a śramaṇī is destroyed, ruined, shattered, fallen, defeated, and her śramaṇahood cannot be recovered. What are the eight?
Listen, O [you] of such-and-such a name: in many ways the Blessed One has censured sensual pleasures—
sensual desire,
sensual affection, sensual love, and the dwelling-place of sensual pleasure.
The restraint of sensual desires,
the relinquishment of sensual desires,
the abandonment of sensual desires has been declared, as well as their renunciation and their utter exhaustion.
It is destruction, dispassion, cessation, tranquility, and disappearance.
It has been praised, extolled, lauded, and commended by me from this day forward: O [Name], you must not look with lustful thoughts at a man’s eyes as he gazes back at yours;
how much less so should you engage in unchaste sexual intercourse through the union of the two organs?

The Blessed One has said: "Furthermore, if a nun who has entered into the commonality of training with the nuns should, without renouncing the training and without disclosing her weakness in the training, engage in unchaste sexual intercourse— even with one born of the animal womb— "
A nun who commits such an offense becomes, by the very fact of that commission, no longer a nun, no longer a Śramaṇī, no longer a daughter of the Śākyas;

she falls from the state of a nun. Her status as a Śramaṇī is destroyed, ruined, shattered, fallen, defeated, and her Śramaṇahood cannot be restored—just as a palm tree cut off at the crown is incapable [of further growth].

Just as a seed that has become rotten is incapable of reaching growth, increase, or abundance, even so, a nun who commits such an offense becomes, by the very act of committing it, no longer a nun, no longer a *śramaṇī*, no longer a daughter of the Śākyas;
she is fallen from the state of a nun. Her state of being a *śramaṇa* is destroyed, ruined, shattered, cast down, and utterly defeated.

Your ascetic life (śrāmaṇya) becomes impossible to reclaim; therefore, from this day forward, while not transgressing, you must apply yourself with intense mental protection, mindfulness, and vigilance to the abstention from transgression. Will you not commit such an act?
I shall not commit it.
Listen, [Name],
in many ways the Blessed One has censured the taking of what is not given and has praised the abstention from taking what is not given.

Praised, lauded, extolled, and glorified from this day forward, you who bear such a name must not, with a mind set on theft, take even as much as a sesame husk belonging to another; how much less so five māṣakas or more than five māṣakas? Thus it was said by the Blessed One.

Furthermore, if a nun should take from others what has not been given—whether in a village or in the wilderness—considered to be theft, such that for the taking of what was not given, a king or a royal minister might seize her and either execute her, imprison her, or banish her, saying to her: "Ho! You man, you are a thief, you are a fool, you are deluded, you are a robber! [then she too is one who has fallen into defeat].

A nun who has committed such an offense becomes, by the very act of committing it, no longer a nun, no longer a śramaṇī, no longer a daughter of the Śākyas—as previously stated—up until: "one must apply oneself to mindfulness and heedfulness.
"Will you not commit such an offense?
"I will not commit it."
Listen, [you] of such-and-such a name: in many ways the Blessed One has censured the taking of life; he has praised, extolled, commended, and lauded abstention from the taking of life.
From this day forward, [you], of such-and-such a name, must not intentionally deprive any living being of life, even down to an ant or an insect;
how much less so a human being or one who has the form of a human?
It was said by the Blessed One:

"Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī should intentionally, with her own hand, deprive a human being or one having human form of life; or if she should provide him with a weapon, or seek out someone to provide him with a weapon; or if she should incite him toward death..."
Or he might describe the praises of death to him and say to him: "Come now, my good man, what use have you for this wretched, impure, and miserable life?

For you, my good man, death is better than life. With thoughts approved by his own mind and through various mental deliberations, he might in many ways incite him toward death or describe the praises of death to him.

If a nun should commit such an offense as this—that he might die by that means—she becomes, upon the very commission of that offense, no longer a nun, no longer a śramaṇī, no longer a daughter of the Śākyas; she falls away from the state of a nun, as previously stated, up until: "one must apply oneself to mindfulness and heedfulness."
"Will you not commit such an act?
"I will not commit it.
"Listen, [Name], in many ways has false speech been censured by the Blessed One."

Abstaining from false speech has been praised, extolled, lauded, and glorified. From this day forward, O [Name], even when joking, you must not speak a deliberate falsehood, let alone prattle about a non-existent, unattainable superhuman state (*uttaramanuṣyadharma*).
And it was said by the Blessed One: "Furthermore, whatever nun, not knowing and not fully understanding, [claims] that which is non-existent and unattainable..."
If one were to claim a superhuman state, an attainment of noble distinction, or knowledge, vision, or a state of abiding in ease—saying "I know this, I see this"—what does one know?
One knows suffering; one knows its origin, its cessation, and the path.
"What do I see? I see gods, I see nāgas, yakṣas, garuḍas, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, piśācas, and kaṭapūtanas.
I hear the voices of the gods; I hear the voices of nāgas, yakṣas, garuḍas, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, pretas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, and kaṭapūtanas."
I approach the gods to see them;
I approach the nāgas, yakṣas, garuḍas, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, pretas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, and kaṭapūtanas to see them.
The gods also approach me to see me.

Nāgas, yakṣas, garuḍas, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, pretas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, and even kaṭapūtanas approach me for the sake of seeing me. I converse with, talk with, and rejoice together with the gods; I even enter into continuous discourse with the nāgas, yakṣas, garuḍas, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, pretas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, and kaṭapūtanas.

I converse, I chat, I exchange greetings, and I even enter into continuous discourse; even the gods converse with me, chat with me, exchange greetings with me, and even enter into continuous discourse.

Nāgas, yakṣas, garuḍas, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, pretas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, and kaṭapūtanas also converse with me, chat with me, exchange greetings with me, and [enter into] continuous discourse.
They do indeed attain them; however,

he who has not yet attained them thinks, "I am one who has attained the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in what is impermanent, the perception of non-self in what is suffering, and [the perception] regarding food."

The perception of repulsiveness, the perception of lack of delight in the entire world, the perception of disadvantage, the perception of abandonment, the perception of dispassion, the perception of death, the perception of cessation,
the perception of impurity, the perception of a livid corpse, the perception of a festering corpse, the perception of a worm-infested corpse, and the perception of a bloated corpse.
He possesses the perception of the devoured, the perception of the bloody-red, the perception of the scattered, the perception of the skeletal, and the perception of the contemplation of emptiness.
He thinks: "I am indeed not an attainer, whereas he is an attainer, of the first dhyāna, the second, the third, and the fourth; of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity;
and of the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception."
"Though I have not actually attained them, I claim: 'I am one who has attained the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning;

I possess the domain of supernormal powers, the divine ear, knowledge of the minds of others, recollection of past lives, knowledge of death and rebirth, and the destruction of the outflows; I am an Arhat, a meditator on the eight liberations, and one liberated both ways.'"
A nun who commits such an offense becomes, by the very fact of that transgression, no longer a nun, no longer a *śramaṇī*, no longer a daughter of the Śākyas;

she falls from the state of a nun. Her status as a *śramaṇī* is destroyed, ruined, shattered, fallen, defeated, and her *śramaṇya* cannot be restored—just as a palmyra tree cut off at the crown is incapable [of further growth].

Just as a seed that has been scorched by fire becomes incapable of greenness, of sprouting, growing, or reaching maturity, even so a nun who commits such an offense ceases to be a nun at the very moment of the offense; she is no longer a *śramaṇī*, no longer a daughter of the Śākyas.
She is fallen from the state of a nun; her status as a *śramaṇī* is destroyed, ruined, shattered, fallen, defeated, and lost.

Your ascetic life becomes impossible to restore; therefore, from this day forward, you must apply yourself with intense mental protection, mindfulness, and heedfulness to the restraint of improper conduct regarding what has been transgressed.
Will you not commit such an act?
"I shall not commit [this offense].
Listen, O [nun] of such-and-such name: it has been said by the Blessed One, 'If a nun, being lustful, should consent to being touched or stroked by a lustful man between the eyes and the knees...'"
A nun who commits such an offense ceases to be a nun by the very fact of that commission; she is no longer a śramaṇī, no longer a daughter of the Śākyas, and is fallen as previously described.
Therefore, one must apply oneself to the restraint of misconduct through intense mental protection, mindfulness, and heedfulness.
Will you not commit such an offense?
I shall not commit [this offense]. Listen, O [Bhikṣuṇī] of such-and-such a name: it has been said by the Blessed One, "If a Bhikṣuṇī, being lustful, should laugh, play, or joke with a lustful man..."
If a nun should make a signal, a sign, or a convention; or should welcome a man coming toward her;

or should cast down a handful [of grain] in such a place where a woman becomes subject to a man—having committed such an act involving these eight points, by that very commission she ceases to be a nun.

"You are not a true ascetic, nor a daughter of the Śākyas," [he said], as before, up until: "You must apply yourself to intense mental protection, mindfulness, and vigilance regarding the avoidance of transgressing the rules of conduct.
Will you not fall into such a state?
"I shall not."

Listen, O [you] of such-and-such a name: it has been said by the Blessed One that if a nun who was previously defeated (pārājikā) and no longer in communion (asaṃvāsyā) should, when she has died, or gone astray, or fled to another country, speak thus: "Previously, noble ladies, I knew in secret that this nun was defeated and no longer in communion."

If a bhikṣuṇī commits such an offense involving the concealment of a fault, by the mere commission of that act she ceases to be a bhikṣuṇī, ceases to be a śramaṇī, and ceases to be a daughter of the Śākyas, as previously stated, up to: "In order to refrain from committing such an offense in the future, one must apply oneself with intense mental protection, mindfulness, and vigilance."
"Will you not fall into such a state?
"I will not.

"Listen, O [Name], it has been said by the Blessed One: 'If a nun, knowing and seeing that a formal act of suspension (utkṣepaṇīya-karman) has been performed against a monk by the complete Saṅgha of monks...'"
And when he has been formally recognized by the entire community of nuns as one who is no longer subject to salutation,

and while he stands within the boundary— pulling out his hair with disheveled locks, causing the hairs on his body to fall from the shock of his agitation, manifesting his submission, and requesting reinstatement— he should be addressed thus: "Noble sir, do not pull out your hair with disheveled locks before the community."
Shave your hair, set forth into homelessness, and do not show respect;

standing within the boundary, request reinstatement. [I shall provide] for the noble one: a bowl, a robe, a carrying-net, a water-strainer, a waist-band, [instruction in] the recitation, the reading, the private study, the yoga, and the mental attention.
"Thinking, 'By whatever means there may be an obstacle for the noble one,
by that very means I shall cause no obstacle,' that bhikṣuṇī should be addressed by the bhikṣuṇīs as follows: 'Noble lady, do not knowingly [act] toward whichever monk...'"
When the formal act of suspension has been performed by the complete Saṃgha, and he has been declared by the complete Bhikṣuṇī-saṃgha as one unworthy of salutation,

then, while he stands within the boundary (sīmā), with his hair disheveled and wild, plucking out his body hair before the Saṃgha, proclaiming his renunciation, and demonstrating his proper conduct, and while requesting reinstatement, speak thus:

Do not, O Noble One, pull out your hair with your hands disheveled; do not cause a shedding of hair in the Saṃgha; do not proclaim your renunciation; do not display the formal salutation; do not, standing within the boundary, request reinstatement. I [shall provide] for the Noble One—by means of his bowl, his robe, his carrying-net, his waist-band, his instruction, his recitation, his study, his yoga, his mental attention, and whatever else belongs to the Noble One.
"There is distress because of this and that; let us bring about freedom from distress. "Noble lady, relinquish such a course of speech as this, which conforms to [the act of] suspension.
If that nun, being thus addressed by the nuns, should relinquish that matter, that is good; if she does not, [she commits an offense].
If she relinquishes it, she should be questioned a second and a third time for the sake of relinquishing that matter;
if, being questioned and instructed a second and a third time, she relinquishes that matter, that is well; but if she does not relinquish it...

If a nun commits such an offense as following one who has been suspended (an-uddhṛta), by the mere commission of that act she ceases to be a nun, ceases to be a śramaṇī, and ceases to be a daughter of the Śākyas, as previously stated, up until the point where she must apply herself with intense mental protection, mindfulness, and vigilance to abstaining from such misconduct. "Will you not commit such an offense? [she is asked].
I shall not transgress.

Listen, [Name], these eight weighty rules (gurudharma) have been prescribed by that Blessed One—the one who knows and sees, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Awakened One—for a bhikṣuṇī who has thus gone forth and received full ordination, as a restriction that must not be overstepped. In this regard:
For as long as life lasts, training must be observed by women.
Which eight?
O [Name], a woman should desire from the presence of the monks the going forth, the full ordination, and the status of a bhikṣuṇī.
"O [you] of such-and-such a name, this is the first *gurudharma* prescribed by the Blessed One for women:
as an obstacle and so that it may not be transgressed, in which the womenfolk must practice the training for as long as life lasts;
from the presence of the monks, the nuns must seek instruction and admonition every half-month."
"O [Name], this is the second heavy rule (gurudharma) prescribed by the Blessed One for women, as an obstruction and for the purpose of non-transgression, in which women must train their lives long.

A nun must not enter the rains retreat in a residence where there is no monk. O [Name], this is the third heavy rule prescribed by the Blessed One for women, as an obstruction and for the purpose of non-transgression, in which women must train their lives long."
A nun who has completed her rains retreat must invite the dual saṃgha [of monks and nuns] by means of three grounds:
what has been seen, what has been heard, and what is suspected.
This, O so-and-so, is the fourth heavy rule (gurudharma) prescribed for women by the Blessed One.
As an obstruction and for the sake of non-transgression, there are certain trainings that must be observed by a woman for as long as she lives:
a nun must not accuse or remind a monk of a failure in morality, a failure in view, a failure in conduct, or a failure in livelihood.
A nun is restricted from accusing or reminding a monk of a failure in morality, a failure in view, or a failure in livelihood;
whereas a monk is unrestricted from accusing or reminding a nun of a failure in morality, a failure in view, or a failure in livelihood.
O so-and-so, this is the fifth *gurudharma* prescribed by the Blessed One for women, as a restriction and an obstacle that must not be transgressed.
In this regard, the training must be observed by a woman for as long as she lives:
a nun must not revile or provoke a monk; it is forbidden for a nun to revile, provoke, or abuse a monk. This, O [Name], is the sixth heavy rule for women established by the Blessed One.
This seventh *gurudharma* has been prescribed by the Blessed One for women as a restriction that must not be transgressed, wherein a woman must practice the training for as long as she lives.
When a nun has committed a *gurudharma*, she must undergo the *mānāpya* penance before both Saṅghas every half-month.
This, O [Name], is the seventh *gurudharma* prescribed by the Blessed One for women as a restriction that must not be transgressed.
In this regard, a woman must observe the training for as long as she lives;

even a nun who has been ordained for a hundred years must perform acts of salutation, prostration, rising to greet, joining of palms, and respectful service toward a monk ordained on that very same day.
"O [Name], this is the eighth *gurudharma* prescribed by the Blessed One for women, for the purpose of restraint and non-transgression, in which a woman must train for as long as she lives.
Do you undertake and abide by these eight *gurudharmas*? "I do."

Listen, [you] whose name is such-and-such: these four, by that Blessed One—[as previously described]—up to: by the Truly Perfectly Awakened One, were declared to be the makers of a nun’s asceticism for a nun who has thus gone forth and received full ordination.
What are the four?
From this day forward, [you] whose name is such-and-such, when reviled, you must not revile in return.
When one is provoked to anger, one should not respond with anger;
when one is struck, one should not strike back; when one is reviled, one should not revile in return.
Listen, O [you] of such-and-such a name: for a long time you have had this aspiration:
"Oh, that I might obtain the going-forth, the full ordination, and the status of a bhikṣuṇī within the well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya!
Now, at this time, [you... (BhīKaVā 31b1)

One who has gone forth and received full ordination— by means of a suitable preceptoress (upādhyāyikā), two suitable teachers (ācāryas), and through a formal act (*karma*) consisting of a motion followed by three proclamations (*jñapticaturtha*), which is irreversible and not subject to suspension— in that very day of ordination, she must train in the training in which a nun ordained for a hundred years must train;
for where one ordained on that day is [treated] as one ordained for a hundred years.
That which is commonality of conduct, commonality of training, and commonality of recitation from the Prātimokṣa-sūtra—this you must fulfill from this day forward and not neglect.
From this day forward, O [Name], you should maintain the perception of your preceptor as a mother; your preceptor, too, should maintain the perception of you as a daughter.
From this day forward, your preceptor must attend to you for as long as life lasts when you are ill, and you must attend to your preceptor when she is ill.
From this day forward, you, [Name], must dwell with reverence,
with respect, with a sense of awe, and with a spirit of submission toward your fellow practitioners of the holy life.
